method: Human-audited prompt calibration from approved references, rejected outputs and marked defect evidence; this is not model fine-tuning.

flat: Use the uploaded garment as the sole authority for construction; never infer an unseen back, inner layer, closure, pocket, label or accessory.
Keep collar, neckline, sleeve length, cuffs, waistband, hem, seams and every visible fastener in the same count, position and topology as the source.
Preserve thin, sheer, glossy, knitted or padded material character; do not make translucent fabric opaque or change apparent thickness.
For multi-piece products, keep every uploaded piece separate, complete and uncropped; never merge pieces or substitute a reference garment.
detail: Magnify only a detail that is visible in authoritative product evidence; do not hallucinate hidden construction.
Preserve the exact count, position, orientation and material of buttons, zippers, belt loops, waist hardware, pockets, labels and decorative elements.
The close-up must remain consistent with the full garment color, weave, stitching direction and surrounding structure.
partial: Generate a native close-up at the requested framing and resolution; never crop or enlarge a full-body output.
Keep the sellable garment fully readable and unobstructed while preserving model identity, natural anatomy and believable garment-body contact.
Do not let fallback base layers introduce outerwear, logos, patterns or accessories that cover or compete with the product.
model: Preserve the complete uploaded outfit manifest and the locked model identity; style references may guide lighting and composition only.
Keep garment length, silhouette, closure, pocket, waistline, hem and layering relationships consistent across the whole body.
Use natural pose, hands, body proportions and garment drape without wide-angle stretching, limb deformation or mannequin stiffness.

negativeAdditions: Do not invent unseen reverse-side details or copy clothing from style references.
Do not change fastener count, pocket placement, collar shape, sleeve length, waistband, hem, transparency, thickness or color.
Do not crop a full-body image to simulate a product close-up.
